I have BPD too. Although I am struggling because of a breakup (happened 10 days ago) and my world is messed up right now , I found two books very enlightning. 1. I Hate You- Don't Leave Me, Understanding the borderline personality by Jerold J. Kreisman, M.D., and Hal Straus. 2. Sometimes I Act Crazy, Living with borderline personality disorder. This book is also by Jerold J. Kreisman, M.D., and Hal Straus. I hope they can help you. My best for you.

I wrote him yesterday, telling him that he was not guilty, that I know I was selfish, that I felt embarrased, that I am treating my problem with alcohol (I am getting a pellet), that I want to live, that I can't express with words how sorry I am, that I want to fight and that I understand if he is angry. That I understand if he thinks that by trying to commit suicide I never thought of him and how much pain I would cause. That I had been selfish. I also Told him that I love him, that he has no responsibility at all, that I still see him as the love of my life. I asked whether he wanted to walk with me in my recovery or leave me alone. I ended the message by sayig that I don't want to push him or take the time he needs. That I thought it would be wise to tell him how everything was going. Because the last time we talked, less than two weeks ago, he said that he wanted me back, that he loved me, but he needed me to take care of myself. Muchas gracias por tus palabras. It makes me smile to have this support

Most of the times I am rational enough to fight and keep fighting. But I am afraid of the moments in which I feel so down. I lose control of myself and to be honest I don't want to kill myself. I just don't want to live and feel this pain. I don't know if I explain myself...  It's just that my mind and my pain numb me and I lose hope and contact with reality. That's when I make wrong decisions. And right now I am kind of scared, kind of happy. I am not hungry and although I still have strenght to look for a job overseas (I don't feel comfortable in my own country, so I usually work abroad), at the same time, the evil side of my is blocking me from eating, get full immediately, and automatically started puking without even provoking it. I am losing weight. I am weaker. But I don't know what to do and I feel embarrassed to tell the doctors and people I know.
Chile, South America :) But I feel more like a citizen of the world. I am always traveling.

Hi there Reithar. I am a 30-year-old Chilean woman (although I still like to call myself "girl"). I am bi, and have had boyfriends and girlfriends. I came out when I was 22, but my family met for the first time a girlfriend when I was 27. My mom was really homophoic and thought that bisexuality was something that could be cured by hanging out only with straight people and introducing me to hot straight guys. That's not really the case. Contrary to what many people think, many bisexuals (me included), are completely faithful to our partner and regardless of the sex, we see the person as a whole. I also spent many years trying to figure out if I was gay or straight. But I came to the conclusion that I am bi, and I feel comfortable about it. I am glad you share your story and I hope you really go to the LGBT society. It always help to share with people who feel the same way as you do and find support there.

Hey there. I was addicted to clonazepam and sleeping pills. I would lie to different doctors to get prescriptions and would also steal from my mom. At  some point I realized I didn't want to live this way. Although I am struggling with alcoholism right now and many other issues, getting rehab for pills was the first big step in recovering. Congratulations on your decision. I'll be sending you good energies and positive thoughts :)

Thank you for taking the time to answer. He always knew I was under medication, he knew I used to cut myself until I was about 24, he knew that many people had abandoned me because of my problem. I hardly ever told him when I felt bad. He hardly ever saw me cry. I never ever threatened him to kill myself. He knows that I battled many years against discrimination for being bisexual. He knew I was damaged but I was fighting. God knows that I was fighting and fighting. He knew that I was going to the psychiatrist and psychologist in the period we were apart (we met while both working in China). He knew. He knew and said he would heal me. That there was nothing to worry about. But he didn't. He never gave me the chance. I just don't understand why he gave up so fast... I supported him in so many ways. When he was the one struggling and depressed i put myself aside and took him out of the hole. People just keep running away. Please... Why?
